article_notes: Korean laboratory submissions (400 dogs with suspected tick-borne disease; 36 B. gibsoni PCR-positive). Severity grouping is the authors' clinical-course classification (acute = complicated form, chronic, subclinical). Table 3 (low/normal/high counts by course) is badly garbled by PDF conversion; the counts were reconstructed by column order and internal sums (see row notes), so confidence is low-medium. Signalment and signs per dog are listed in Table 2 but no group summaries or tests are printed for them, so they are not extracted. Table 1 compares PCR/antibody positivity by region, sex, age (and breed in a supplement): infection risk, not severity; counted as skipped. Samples taken at the referring clinic; treatment timing not stated.

severity_definitions.label: acute (complicated form) vs chronic (mild, non-specific) vs subclinical (apparently healthy)
severity_definitions.definition: 34 PCR-positive B. gibsoni dogs classed by clinical signs from the submitting clinic's records: Group I acute = signs of the complicated form (n=19), Group II chronic = mild to non-specific signs (n=11), Group III subclinical = apparently healthy (n=4). Labs available for 15/8/3. No explicit criteria list; complications named in Table 2 include IMHA and pancreatitis ('other').
severity_definitions.comparison_group: chronic infection (n=8 with labs; 11 overall) and subclinical (n=3 with labs; 4 overall)
severity_definitions.quote: dogs manifesting symptoms of the complicated form of canine babesiosis (Group I – acute infection), dogs with mild to non-specific symptoms (Group II – chronic infection), and apparently healthy dogs (Group III – subclinical infection)
